newsitem.title: SPAIN: Mayor from ETA's political wing ousted in Spain.
newsitem.headline: Mayor from ETA's political wing ousted in Spain.

text.p: Mainstream politicians in Spain's Basque region ousted a separatist mayor on Thursday, loosening the longtime grip on local governments of the guerrilla group ETA's political wing.
In a tense session, the town council in the Basque nationalist stronghold Mondragon voted 13-6 with two abstentions to replace Xabier Zubizarreta of ETA's political arm Herri Batasuna.
Appointed in his place was Jose Maria Loiti of the more moderate Basque Nationalist Party.
ETA sympathisers carrying posters of imprisoned rebels chanted support for Herri Batasuna outside the town hall and jeered the other politicians, drowning out the words of the newly elected Loiti.
"The people will not forgive," they shouted.
The councillors' motion accused Herri Batasuna of using town halls in the northern region as "platforms of destabilisation of the system".

ETA, which has slain some 800 people in nearly three decades of fighting for Basque independence, sparked national outrage last month by brutally killing a young Basque town councillor 48 hours after kidnapping him.
Political leaders in the autonomous Basque region accused Herri Batasuna of complicity in the murder of 29-year-old Miguel Angel Blanco and took steps to curb its political clout.

Despite a growing revulsion at ETA's tactics, the radical separatist movement still has bedrock support in many villages. Zubizarreta had been mayor of Mondragon, the largest town headed by Herri Batasuna, for 10 years.

More than 20,000 pro-ETA demonstrators led by Herri Batasuna marched through San Sebastian three weeks after an estimated six million Spaniards took to the streets in angry protest at Blanco's killing.
